_comment: Shared test vectors for roster-address canonicalization -- the ONE notion of
"the same address" used by BOTH the console validator
_canonicalize_roster_entry). This fixture is the ARBITER: both suites load it
and assert their own real implementation maps every input to its expected
WHY IT EXISTS (ss#2284). The two disagreed. The validator did a bare
trim().toLowerCase() while the runtime NFC-normalized, so NFD and NFC
spellings of one accented address passed the validator's collision rules as
two addresses and resolved at runtime to one -- one human holding two silent
exposure classes. They also used different whitespace sets: JavaScript's
\s covers NBSP, the ideographic space and the BOM; the Python list did not.
Measured on both real implementations before the fix: 4 of 10 probe cases
Adding a case here is how the rule changes. Both suites fail until both
languages follow, which is the whole point -- neither copy can drift alone.
Inputs are synthetic; no real roster address appears.

cases.name: NFD decomposed accent normalizes to the SAME address as its NFC twin (the ss#2284 defect: two spellings, one human, two exposure classes)
non-breaking space inside the local part
ideographic space inside the local part
byte-order mark inside the local part
NEL (C1 control) inside the local part
unit separator (C0 control) inside the local part
whole-domain grant with a non-breaking space -- the ONLY path the roster-entry check guards alone, since an @domain entry returns before _canonicalize_address ever sees it
